textbookText: v) Due to the Earth's orbiting motion, it experiences centrifugal force, resulting in flattening at the poles and bulging at the equator. 6.1.2 Angular Displacement and Velocity Activity 6.2 i) Create the largest possible circular path on your school ground using a chalk mark. ii) Stand at a point marked as A on the path with a stopwatch, and begin moving around the circle. iii) Stop at a point on the circle, marking it as B, before completing the circle, and note the time it took to reach there as ’t’. iv) Measure the distance between points A and B using a string, naming it as’s’. Then, connect points A and B with the center O of the constructed circle. Measure the angle subtended by AB at the center and name it as θ. v) Begin your new journey from the initial point A once more, completing a cycle. Note the time taken and designate it as T. Repeat this process for two complete cycles, noting the total time as 2T. Then, continue by completing three full cycles, recording the total time taken as 3T, and so forth. vi) The time T has a special feature and try to recognize it. Imagine the swift motion involving multiple complete cycles within a second and attempt to comprehend it. Here, the distance’s’ between two points represents the linear distance, while the angle 'θ' denotes the angular displacement. The ratio of angular displacement to time ('θ/t') yields the angular velocity 'ω', and the time 'T' required for a complete oscillation defines the period. Furthermore, the frequency 'f' corresponds to the number of cycles completed in one second.

Angular Velocity: It is the rate of change of angular displacement and is denoted by ω, read as omega. Therefore, Angular Velocity = angular displacement / time ∴ ω = θ/t For the instantaneous value of ω, ω = lim ∆θ = dθ ∆t dt Δt→0 Unit of ω ω = θ/t = rad/second = rads-1 Angular Acceleration: The rate of change of angular velocity is the angular acceleration. i.e Angular Acceleration, Angular Velocity Change α = time = ω− ω0 t » ω = ω0 + αt. Time Period: The time taken by a particle to make a complete oscillation is the time period, T. From ω = 𝜃, take θ = 2π for a complete oscillation and t = T for that. 𝑡 ∴ ω =2π.
